metadata.title: Impact of Undertreated Antithrombotic Therapy on Adverse Patient Outcomes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
top_takeaways: Antithrombotic undertreatment—including therapy omission, subtherapeutic underdosing, and nonadherence—drives significant increases in ischemic stroke, recurrent thrombosis, systemic embolism, and all-cause mortality across conditions such as atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and peripheral artery disease.

Deviations from evidence-based guideline dosing are commonly driven by clinician misperceptions regarding bleeding versus thrombotic risk, alongside healthcare access barriers magnified by social determinants of health.

Implementation of interprofessional antithrombotic stewardship programs provides a structured, evidence-based mechanism to bridge care gaps, optimize therapeutic dosing, and improve clinical outcomes.

recommendations.statement: In patients with indications for antithrombotic therapy—including atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and peripheral artery disease—evidence-based guideline-recommended dosing should be maintained, and inappropriate dose reductions or therapy omissions driven by unfounded bleeding concerns should be avoided.
